newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold, silver end lower on dull demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold, silver end lower on dull demand.

text.p: ** Standard gold 24 carats close 10 rupees lower at 4,795 rupees per 10 grammes on slack demand and a downtrend in international prices. It opened 5.0 rupees higher at 4,810 rupees per 10 grammes.
** Gold biscuits (116.50 grammes) end 100 rupees lower at 56,200 rupees per piece. Gold biscuits opened 100 rupees higher at 56,300 rupees per piece.
** Silver (.999) closes 55 rupees lower at 6,855 rupees per kg. It opened steady at 6,910 rupees per kg.

Standard gold 24 carats lost the gains from early trade on poor demand to close 10 rupees lower at 4,795 rupees per 10 grammes. It opened 5.0 rupees higher over the previous closing of 4,810 rupees per 10 grammes.
"Demand slackened during the day's trading. It was one of those fluctuations," said Bombay Bullion Association president Makhan Lal Damani.
Damani said local sentiment was subdued in response to a downtrend in international prices.
"When world prices are down, buyers adopt a wait-and-watch policy, hoping the prices might fall further," he said.
Gold biscuits (116.50 grammes) lost 100 rupees to 56,200 rupees per piece. They opened 100 rupees higher at 56,300 rupees per piece.
Silver .999 lost 55 rupees to 6,855 rupees per kg after opening steady at 6,910 rupees per kg.
"Heavy arrivals, coulpled with dull demand brought silver prices down," Damani said.
He said heavy imports of silver by traders in India's western city of Ahmedabad and the Indian capital city of New Delhi had flodded the markets there.
"These imports have cast an adverse impact on the local market," Damani said. "But sentiment should improve in the next few days because of marriage season demand." (Conversion $1=35.74 rupees)
